REGIONAL REGULATION

REGIONAL REGULATION

WEST BANDUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2015

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF WEST BANDUNG,

Considering : a. that women and children are national assets who play a role in the process of succession and creation of quality generations and need to obtain guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination; b. that based on Article 7 paragraph (2) letter n of Government Regulation Number 38 of 2007 concerning the Division of Governmental Affairs Between the Government, Provincial Regional Government and Regency/Municipal Regional Government, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are governmental affairs that must be organized by the Regional Government; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; In view of : 1. Article 18 Paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1974 Number 1, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3019); 3. Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1984 Number 29, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3277); 4. Law Number 20 of 1999 concerning Ratification of ILO Convention No. 138 Concerning Minimum Age for Admission to Employment (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 56, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3835); 5. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 6. Law Number 1 of 2000 concerning Ratification of ILO Convention No. 182 Concerning The Prohibition and Immediate Action for the Elimination of the Worst Forms of Child Labour (State Gazette of 2000 Number 30, Supplement to the State Gazette Number 3941); 7. Article 20

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 18 letter b, are implemented in the form of community participation.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling victims of acts of violence.

Article 21

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 18 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 25

(1) The form of service as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regional Government in accordance with the minimum service standards established by the Government.

(2) In the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may cooperate with government agencies, provincial government, other regency/city governments, law enforcement officers, and the community.

(3) Further provisions regarding procedures for services and handling of women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 26

(1) In order to provide protection services for women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center in implementing programs and activities for the protection of women and children.

(2) The Establishment, Organization, and Working Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 29

(1) The Task Force as referred to in Article 28 letter a, consists of representatives from the Regional Government, Law Enforcement, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Professional Organizations, and Researchers/Academics.

(2) The Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution that has the task of coordinating programs and activities for the prevention and handling of victims of violence against Women and Children, and Human Trafficking.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organization, duties and functions of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender as an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life, hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP, is an effort to improve women's physical and mental conditions in fulfilling their rights and living needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection against trafficking in children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the unequal relationship patterns between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that responds to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement, hereinafter abbreviated as GBS, is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or that a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap issues. 15. Focal Point PUG is a SKPD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development, hereinafter referred to as BKB, is a community movement aimed at increasing parents' knowledge and skills in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Mother Care Movement, hereinafter referred to as GSI, is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rate (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rate (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced and Independent Indonesian Women, hereinafter referred to as Model Desa PRIMA, is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reducing the burden of health and education costs for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Enhancement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families, hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS, is an integrated program to enhance women's role that uses a coordinated cross-sectoral development approach pattern to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center for women's empowerment efforts in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination forum that aims to ensure the implementation of prevention and handling of the crime of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

Article 28

In addition to establishing P2TP2A as referred to in Article 26, in order to support the implementation of the protection of women and children, the Regent establishes:

a. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Victims of Violence Against Women, Victims of Violence Against Children, and Human Trafficking;
b. Regional Action Committee for the Elimination of the Worst Forms of Child Labor.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 27

(1) P2TP2A has the main task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, appropriate and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.

(2) In carrying out the tasks as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the functions:

a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature quickly covering various services, namely information, medical referrals, legal, psychological, psychic, safe houses (shelters), home visits, and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

REGIONAL REGULATION

WEST BANDUNG REGENCY

NUMBER 3 OF 2015

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

AND CHILD PROTECTION

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF WEST BANDUNG,

Considering : a. that women and children are national assets who play a role in the process of succession and creation of quality generations and need to obtain guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination; b. that based on Article 7 paragraph (2) letter n of Government Regulation Number 38 of 2007 concerning the Division of Governmental Affairs Between the Government, Provincial Regional Government and Regency/Municipal Regional Government, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are governmental affairs that must be organized by the Regional Government; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; In view of : 1. Law Number 20 of 1999 concerning Ratification of ILO Convention No. 138 Concerning Minimum Age for Admission to Employment (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 56, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3835); 5. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 6. Law Number 1 of 2000 concerning Ratification of ILO Convention No. 182 Concerning The Prohibition and Immediate Action for the Elimination of the Worst Forms of Child Labour (State Gazette of 2000 Number 30, Supplement to the State Gazette Number 3941); 7. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4235), as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606); 8. Law Number 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 39, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 9. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95); 10. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender as an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life, hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP, is an effort to improve women's physical and mental conditions in fulfilling their rights and living needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection against trafficking in children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the unequal relationship patterns between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that responds to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Toddler Family Development, hereinafter referred to as BKB, is a community movement aimed at increasing parents' knowledge and skills in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Mother Care Movement, hereinafter referred to as GSI, is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rate (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rate (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced and Independent Indonesian Women, hereinafter referred to as Model Desa PRIMA, is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reducing the burden of health and education costs for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Enhancement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families, hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS, is an integrated program to enhance women's role that uses a coordinated cross-sectoral development approach pattern to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center for women's empowerment efforts in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination forum that aims to ensure the implementation of prevention and handling of the crime of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

(1) In order to provide protection services for women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center in implementing programs and activities for the protection of women and children.

Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 18 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Focal Point PUG is a SKPD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

Part Four

Institutional Framework for the Protection of Women and Children

Article 27

(1) P2TP2A has the main task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, appropriate and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.

(2) In carrying out the tasks as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the functions:

a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature quickly covering various services, namely information, medical referrals, legal, psychological, psychic, safe houses (shelters), home visits, and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

Programs and Activities for the Protection of Women and Children

1.8.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender as an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life, hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP, is an effort to improve women's physical and mental conditions in fulfilling their rights and living needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection against trafficking in children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the unequal relationship patterns between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that responds to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement, hereinafter abbreviated as GBS, is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or that a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap issues. 15. Focal Point PUG is a SKPD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development, hereinafter referred to as BKB, is a community movement aimed at increasing parents' knowledge and skills in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Mother Care Movement, hereinafter referred to as GSI, is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rate (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rate (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced and Independent Indonesian Women, hereinafter referred to as Model Desa PRIMA, is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reducing the burden of health and education costs for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Enhancement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families, hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS, is an integrated program to enhance women's role that uses a coordinated cross-sectoral development approach pattern to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center for women's empowerment efforts in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination forum that aims to ensure the implementation of prevention and handling of the crime of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

Article 27

(1) P2TP2A has the main task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, appropriate and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.

(2) In carrying out the tasks as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the functions:

a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature quickly covering various services, namely information, medical referrals, legal, psychological, psychic, safe houses (shelters), home visits, and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

Article 29

(1) The Task Force as referred to in Article 28 letter a, consists of representatives from the Regional Government, Law Enforcement, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Professional Organizations, and Researchers/Academics.

(2) The Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution that has the task of coordinating programs and activities for the prevention and handling of victims of violence against Women and Children, and Human Trafficking.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organization, duties and functions of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 28

In addition to establishing P2TP2A as referred to in Article 26, in order to support the implementation of the protection of women and children, the Regent establishes:

a. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Victims of Violence Against Women, Victims of Violence Against Children, and Human Trafficking;
b. Regional Action Committee for the Elimination of the Worst Forms of Child Labor.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender as an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life, hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP, is an effort to improve women's physical and mental conditions in fulfilling their rights and living needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection against trafficking in children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the unequal relationship patterns between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that responds to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement, hereinafter abbreviated as GBS, is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or that a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap issues. 15. Focal Point PUG is a SKPD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development, hereinafter referred to as BKB, is a community movement aimed at increasing parents' knowledge and skills in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Mother Care Movement, hereinafter referred to as GSI, is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rate (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rate (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced and Independent Indonesian Women, hereinafter referred to as Model Desa PRIMA, is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reducing the burden of health and education costs for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Enhancement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families, hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS, is an integrated program to enhance women's role that uses a coordinated cross-sectoral development approach pattern to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center for women's empowerment efforts in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination forum that aims to ensure the implementation of prevention and handling of the crime of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

Part Three

Programs and Activities for the Protection of Women and Children

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender as an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life, hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP, is an effort to improve women's physical and mental conditions in fulfilling their rights and living needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection against trafficking in children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the unequal relationship patterns between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that responds to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement, hereinafter abbreviated as GBS, is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or that a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap issues. 15. Focal Point PUG is a SKPD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development, hereinafter referred to as BKB, is a community movement aimed at increasing parents' knowledge and skills in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Mother Care Movement, hereinafter referred to as GSI, is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rate (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rate (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced and Independent Indonesian Women, hereinafter referred to as Model Desa PRIMA, is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reducing the burden of health and education costs for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Enhancement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families, hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS, is an integrated program to enhance women's role that uses a coordinated cross-sectoral development approach pattern to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center for women's empowerment efforts in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination forum that aims to ensure the implementation of prevention and handling of the crime of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Article 34

Guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 33, are implemented in order to realize the objectives of implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in accordance with the minimum service standards established by the Government.

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 27

(1) P2TP2A has the main task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, appropriate and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.

(2) In carrying out the tasks as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the functions:

a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature quickly covering various services, namely information, medical referrals, legal, psychological, psychic, safe houses (shelters), home visits, and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

(2) The monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in every SKPD.

(4) The implementation of evaluation may be conducted through cooperation with Universities, Women's Study Centers, or Non-Governmental Organizations for Women's Empowerment and Protection.

(5) The results of the evaluation of PUG implementation serve as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the coming year.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women. 6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender as an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Article 27

(1) P2TP2A has the main task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, appropriate and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.

(2) In carrying out the tasks as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the functions:

a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature quickly covering various services, namely information, medical referrals, legal, psychological, psychic, safe houses (shelters), home visits, and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Women and Children; and

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the unequal relationship patterns between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that responds to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement, hereinafter abbreviated as GBS, is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or that a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap issues. 15. Focal Point PUG is a SKPD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development, hereinafter referred to as BKB, is a community movement aimed at increasing parents' knowledge and skills in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Mother Care Movement, hereinafter referred to as GSI, is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rate (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rate (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced and Independent Indonesian Women, hereinafter referred to as Model Desa PRIMA, is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reducing the burden of health and education costs for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Enhancement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families, hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS, is an integrated program to enhance women's role that uses a coordinated cross-sectoral development approach pattern to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center for women's empowerment efforts in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons is a cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination forum that aims to ensure the implementation of prevention and handling of the crime of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25.

Article 27

(1) P2TP2A has the main task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, appropriate and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.

(2) In carrying out the tasks as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the functions:

a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature quickly covering various services, namely information, medical referrals, legal, psychological, psychic, safe houses (shelters), home visits, and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter referred to as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results or may result in physical, sexual or psychological suffering or harm to women, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in physical, mental, sexual, psychological suffering or harm, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the integrated service provider to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is an action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is a legal service provided by legal companions and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 26

(1) In order to provide protection services for women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center in implementing programs and activities for the protection of women and children.

(2) The Establishment, Organization, and Working Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 18 letter b, are implemented in the form of community participation.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling victims of acts of violence.

Article 25

(1) The form of service as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by the Regional Government in accordance with the minimum service standards established by the Government.

(2) In the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may cooperate with government agencies, provincial government, other regency/city governments, law enforcement officers, and the community.

(3) Further provisions regarding procedures for services and handling of women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 29

(1) The Task Force as referred to in Article 28 letter a, consists of representatives from the Regional Government, Law Enforcement, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Professional Organizations, and Researchers/Academics.

(2) The Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution that has the task of coordinating programs and activities for the prevention and handling of victims of violence against Women and Children, and Human Trafficking.

(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organization, duties and functions of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Human Trafficking as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.
